title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Chapter IX of the July 1986 notes on 'ateliers' (workshops). From the surrounding pages, an atelier appears to be a set A with three relations:
- a 'smallness/inclusion' relation ◁ (or ⊂);
- a 'strict/interior containment' relation ≪°;
- an 'incompatibility/disjointness' relation |∘|.
These satisfy axioms Ax1–Ax4. To an atelier A one attaches a 'set of points' Σ_A, itself carrying a disjointness relation |∘|.

Conversely, starting from such a Σ, the previous page builds At_spat(Σ), which this page apparently calls Atspl(Σ). Its elements are 'elementary spatial pairs' (L, ρ): L is a family of elements of Σ with a greatest element, and ρ is an order. The three relations are defined as follows:
- ◁ is induced from At_ens(Σ).
- (L,ρ) ≪° (L',ρ') means there is a monotone map φ: L → L' with X ≤ φ(X), sending greatest element to greatest element.
- |∘| means the two greatest elements are themselves |∘|-related in Σ, not merely distinct.

This page does three things.

(1) Axioms. Grothendieck records that axioms 1–4 hold trivially ('Clair') for At_spat(Σ). So it is an atelier, and he presumes a spatial one.

(2) Comparison with the earlier notion. Set A = At_spat(Σ). Define A → Σ by X = (Φ,ρ) ↦ X^0, the greatest element of Φ. Under this map the relation |∘| on A induces the given relation on Σ, by the very definition of |∘| on A. Hence there is an injective map Σ_A → Σ_Σ = Σ, where Σ is regarded as its own space of points.

(3) A section. Conversely, define Σ → A by x ↦ ({x}, ρ_x), with ρ_x the unique order on a singleton. The relation |∘| on Σ is induced from that on A, and the composite Σ → A → Σ is the identity.

Where this leads (next page): Σ_A ≅ Σ. The canonical map A → Atspl(Σ_A) is then identified with the identity, hence is a bijection. For an arbitrary atelier A, the map X ↦ Disp(X) gives a faithful morphism A → Atspl(Σ_A), with X ⊂ Y iff Disp X ⊂ Disp Y. A is 'spatial' exactly when this morphism is an isomorphism.

In modern terms this is a representation theorem of Stone / sober-space / spatial-locale type:
- a 'points' functor Σ_(–) and a 'realisation' functor Atspl(–);
- the realisation of a point-structure is spatial and recovers its points (Σ_{Atspl Σ} ≅ Σ);
- every atelier embeds faithfully into the realisation of its points, with equality characterising spatiality.
It is an adjunction-like duality restricted to its fixed points.
errors: The step 'on trouve donc une application injective Σ_A → Σ' is asserted without explaining how a map A → Σ induces a map on point sets, i.e. why points of A, presumably maximal/elementary elements or filters, are carried to points of Σ. Injectivity is justified only on the next page, via the section Σ → A.
Previous page: the parenthetical '(ce qui est plus fort, sauf pour X, X' ≠ 0_Σ)' presumably should read '= 0_Σ' or similar, a slip. Not on this page.
On this page At_spat(Σ) is called 'At spl'/'Atspl'. The notation is not quite consistent with the previous page's At_spat, though the meaning is clear.

ideas.what: Verification that the canonical construction At_spat(Σ) from a set with a disjointness relation satisfies the atelier axioms
ideas.modern_name: Realisation of a point-structure as an abstract 'region' structure (cf. region-based / mereotopological structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereotopology / region-connection calculi (Whitehead, de Laguna; later Clarke, Randell–Cui–Cohn); in order theory, standard

ideas.what: Map A → Σ (greatest element) and section Σ → A (singletons) showing Σ_{Atspl(Σ)} ≅ Σ
ideas.modern_name: Unit/counit of a points–realisation adjunction being an iso on spatial/sober objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); locale theory (Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone 'Stone Spaces' 1982)

ideas.what: Faithful embedding of any atelier A into Atspl(Σ_A) via X ↦ Disp(X); 'spatial' = this is an isomorphism (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Stone-type representation theorem; spatial vs non-spatial (cf. spatial locales, sobrification)

missed.claim: The 'ateliers' theory itself is an unpublished axiomatics of spatial regions/configurations with incompatibility and interior-containment relations, together with a Stone-type representation theorem. To my knowledge it appears nowhere in Grothendieck's published or circulated texts. The content of this page alone is routine verification.
missed.quote: Ax 1 Clair ... Ax 4 Clair. ... le composé Σ → A → Σ est l'identité.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest unless the full atelier axioms (elsewhere in the dossier) turn out to anticipate mereotopology or point-free topology in a non-trivial way. The representation step here is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page records routine checks: the axioms hold trivially, and a points/realisation round trip is the identity, which is the standard step in a Stone/sober-type duality. The broader 'ateliers' framework is unpublished and mildly curious, but nothing on this page goes beyond well-known representation-theorem patterns.
transcription_corrections: '𝒜t opt(Σ)' should be read as 'Atspl(Σ)' / 'At spat(Σ)', the spatial atelier of the previous page.
The relation written '|·|' is the incompatibility relation '|∘|' of the previous page.
In 'la relation de ... dans Σ' the missing words are presumably 'la relation |∘| donnée dans Σ'.

Before 'la relation |∘| sur Σ soit induite...' the image suggests an inserted 'telle que' / 'Il est clair que'. The sense is: the relation on Σ is induced via x ↦ ({x},ρ_x), and Σ → A → Σ is the identity.
Under 'Σ_Σ = Σ' there is a small marginal gloss, illegible, possibly 'comme on vient de voir'.
Opening line: 'Voyons quel est le rapport avec [la notion] précédente d'ateliers' (struck words in between).
